quote: It's really quite exploratory, but what can you tell me?
stewart_read: The customer directly invites the rep to explain, which is also the interest-reason moment. Rep pivots to describing the design process rather than first asking what specifically got him interested, losing a chance to anchor emotionally on his stated motivation before qualifying.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be following script order (verify before interest) and simply hadn't reached the interest question yet — but the rep does ask it moments later at 00:43, so the omission here is not fatal.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly acknowledge the customer's own framing ('exploratory... what can you tell me') before pivoting to process, so the customer feels heard before being qualified.

quote: On the average, I'd say it's somewhere around $400. Okay. Our last bill because of the weather and the gift was, 600.
stewart_read: Strong bill capture — customer gives both an average and a peak figure unprompted. Rep acknowledges it lightly ('Yeah. Dang.') but never flips it into an emotional case for acting now.
coaching_implication: This is the clearest missed flip on the call — see bill_anchor_audit for detail.

quote: Our service are is a dual service of two, 200 amp panels. We we consume a lot of electricity.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a technical detail (dual 200-amp panel service) indicating unusually high electrical capacity/consumption. This is a qualifying/sizing signal the rep could reflect back to build anticipation for a larger system, not just log silently.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as an enthusiasm signal (higher usage = bigger opportunity), but the customer's tone and content here are matter-of-fact technical description rather than excitement, so it reads more as underused qualifying data than a missed emotional cue.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reflect high-usage disclosures back to the customer ('with that kind of load, this is exactly the type of home solar makes the biggest difference for') to build anticipation for the closer's presentation.

quote: So, yeah, let's see. If 3,000 is kind of the average throughout the year Yeah. Yeah. I'll just do the math there. So 3,000 times 12 will tell us kind of your annual your annual usage there.
stewart_read: The customer's explanation of his usage figures was genuinely garbled (he restates and self-corrects mid-sentence), so it's unclear whether 3,000 kWh was meant as an annual or monthly figure. The rep proceeds to multiply by 12 without confirming, which risks passing an inflated number to the design team, but this is a flagged risk to verify rather than a confirmed error given the ambiguity in what the customer actually said.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have correctly caught an ambiguous customer statement and made a reasonable interpretation in the moment; without hearing the audio inflection, this can't be called a clear-cut math error.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to slow down and repeat back usage figures for confirmation ('so to be clear, you're using about 3,000 kWh total for the year, is that right?') before doing math on ambiguous customer numbers, since this feeds directly into the design accuracy.

quote: And is this a phone number that can receive a text message?
stewart_read: The customer's reply is confused — he says the number 'is not' able to receive texts, then reverses and gives a number anyway prefaced by 'I've gotta give you our cell phone for testing,' which is unclear in meaning. The rep does not clarify whose number this is or confirm it will actually work for texting, creating a real risk that the confirmation text never reaches anyone.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to slow down and explicitly confirm ambiguous customer statements about phone numbers before ending the call — a garbled number-capture step directly undermines the button-up text-confirmation protocol.

quote: Can you I'm I wanna put my wife on the cell on the speaker.
stewart_read: Customer voluntarily loops in his wife for scheduling. Rep responds warmly and naturally ('My wife is the same way. I completely understand.') without turning it into friction, which is correct protocol handling.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example — rep matched tone and didn't treat the spouse addition as an obstacle. Reinforce this instinct.
